title: Module Tor amplitude is equivalent to a bounded flat model
statement: Let A be a ring, let M^\bullet be a cochain complex of A-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and let a\le b be integers. The complex M^\bullet has Tor amplitude in [a,b], meaning that H^i(M^\bullet\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N)=0 for every A-module N and every i\notin[a,b], if and only if there are a cochain complex P^\bullet of flat A-modules, with P^i=0 for i\notin[a,b], and an isomorphism M^\bullet\cong P^\bullet in D(A) [def-pc-derived-category].

proof.text: Specialize the proved generic theorem DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn_iff_exists_iso_Q_obj_flat to C = ModuleCat A and K = Q.obj M. The instance ModuleCat.hasFunctorialFlatResolution supplies the required resolution hypothesis.

For every module N, categorical flatness is equivalent to Module.Flat A N: ObjectProperty.flat_iff_preservesFiniteLimits identifies both with finite-limit preservation of tensorLeft N, via Module.Flat.iff_preservesFiniteLimits_tensorLeft. Convert the generic theorem termwise.

Convert IsStrictlyGE and IsStrictlyLE to termwise vanishing using the support lemmas, reverse the derived isomorphism, and apply the generic equivalence in both directions. The fixed hab hypothesis is unused because the generic theorem does not require ordering.
